P0800.title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
P0800.description: P0800 works like P0700 for the transmission: the transfer case control module has detected a fault of its own that it rates as emissions-relevant and asks the engine control module to turn on the MIL. The engine module only stores P0800; the actual fault – often C, U or manufacturer codes – sits in the transfer case module and needs a scan tool that addresses it. CARB requires monitoring of an electronic transfer case only where it feeds other diagnostics, for example the 4WD-low signal that GM uses as an enable condition; this is why most transfer case modules never request the MIL and P0800 hardly appears in manufacturer documents. A GM bulletin for 2020–23 trucks with 'Service 4WD' and the MIL points to wiring and terminal contact at the transfer case.

causes.label: Fault in the transfer case system stored in its module (shift motor, sensor, clutch)
Wiring or connector at the transfer case (terminal tension, corrosion)
Transfer case module software
Transfer case module faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
'Service 4WD' or similar warning
All-wheel drive or low range cannot be selected

P0801.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit/Open
P0801.description: On GM manual gearboxes (Tremec T56/TR6060 in Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V and ATS-V) the engine module drives a solenoid that blocks reverse while the car moves forward. P0801 means its control circuit is open. GM's tables describe the check: the low-side driver's internal diagnosis flags an open line with at least 9 V and the engine above 250 rpm, 20 failures in 25 samples of 250 ms – about 6 s; in 2006 a 5 s comparison of commanded and actual driver state. GM rates it type C, emissions-neutral and without MIL, from 2019 with a 'service vehicle soon' note. Depending on how it fails, reverse cannot be engaged or is no longer blocked. The title was updated to the current J2012 wording with '/Open'.

causes.label: Connector at the reverse inhibit solenoid loose or corroded
Solenoid coil open
Harness between engine module and gearbox damaged
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Reverse hard or impossible to engage
Reverse no longer blocked
Service note in the driver display, usually no MIL

P0802.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
P0802.description: On older vehicles with a separate transmission module and no MIL message on the CAN bus, the transmission module signals 'MIL on' over its own wire to the engine module. P0802 checks this wire for an open circuit. GM's Duramax tables of 2004 and 2005 (Allison 1000) describe it: at key-on the transmission module briefly pulls the line active like a bulb check; if the engine module sees no off-to-on transition between 0.125 and 7 s after ignition, the line is treated as open – type B, MIL after two trips. Only then is P0700 evaluated. The wire itself must be monitored because an open line would stop transmission emission faults from lighting the MIL. Newer vehicles send the request over CAN, where faults appear as U codes.

causes.label: MIL request wire or connector between the modules open or corroded
Transmission module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Module output or input faulty
Wrong or retrofitted transmission module without this line

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Transmission faults no longer light the MIL
Usually no change in driving

P0803.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit
P0803.description: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid in the shifter housing that, at light load and low speed blocks the way from 1st into 2nd and 3rd so the driver shifts 1 to 4 – a measure for fuel economy ratings; the 1-4 lamp (P0804) shows it. P0803 means the solenoid control circuit is open. GM's tables check the low-side driver while it is off: too low a voltage or over 200 kΩ to ground, with at least 9 V and over 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms (2019 LT5: 20 of 25), type B with the MIL after two trips; shorts are P080C and P080D. An open circuit leaves the solenoid unpowered, so 1 to 2 always works. 'Skip-shift eliminators' with the wrong resistance are a frequent cause.

causes.label: Solenoid unplugged or replaced by a skip-shift eliminator with the wrong resistance
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
Solenoid coil open
Harness damaged
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips
1-4 lockout no longer works (1-2 always possible)
Otherwise no change in driving

P0804.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit
P0804.description: With GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes, a '1-4' lamp in the cluster tells the driver that the lockout is active and to shift from 1st directly into 4th. P0804 means the control circuit of this lamp is faulty – open, shorted, or the lamp does not follow its command. No GM table from 2004 to 2025 available to us contains it, because newer cars switch the indicator by a CAN message from the instrument cluster without a separate engine-module line check; the code therefore mainly concerns older vehicles with a lamp driven directly by the engine module. The lockout itself (P0803) keeps working, only the hint is missing; there is no limp mode, and the MIL behavior is not documented.

causes.label: Bulb or LED in the cluster faulty
Wire or connector between engine module and cluster open or shorted
Instrument cluster board faulty
Engine module output faulty

symptoms: 1-4 lamp never lights or stays on
Possibly check engine lamp
Lockout works without the hint

P0805.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit
P0805.description: The J2012 family 'Clutch Position Sensor A' (P0805 circuit, P0806 range/performance, P0807 low, P0808 high, P0809 intermittent, P080A not learned) covers the position of a clutch – the pedal of a manual gearbox, the clutch actuator of an automated or dual-clutch gearbox, or a clutch inside an automatic. P0805 is the general circuit fault. Uses differ: Nissan's 2022 Pathfinder with its nine-speed automatic stores it in the transmission module, lights the MIL and disables idle stop ('Idle Stop System Fault'), fixed with new software. Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the module-internal chip that drives the clutch A motor, so a control unit fault rather than an outside sensor. GM reads its clutch pedal sensor under P0806–P0808 only.

causes.label: Clutch position sensor faulty (pedal or actuator)
Connector or harness open, corroded or shorted
Transmission module software (Nissan)
Control unit internal fault (Ford DPS6: clutch motor driver)

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Idle stop disabled ('Idle Stop System Fault')
Jerky driving or harsh clutch engagement (dual clutch)

P0806.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0806.description: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0806 is the plausibility check. On GM's LT4 manual cars the pedal sensor is compared with gear detection: if it reports the clutch pressed while engine and output speed show a valid gear, a filtered position error above 4 % sets the code (above 5.6 mph, not in 4WD low), type A with the MIL after one trip. On Ford's DPS6 it reports a fault of the Hall sensors on the clutch A motor; Saab sets it for a frozen pedal signal and switches off cruise control.

causes.label: Pedal sensor or Hall sensors of the clutch motor faulty
Pedal sensor misadjusted or not relearned after clutch work
Harness or connector with contact resistance
Clutch actuator motor faulty (DPS6)
Master cylinder leaking, pedal does not fully return

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control and start-stop not working
Engine starts only with the pedal fully pressed, or not at all
Dual clutch: jerky take-off, limp mode

P0807.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0807.description: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0807 means the signal is too low. GM's three-wire pedal sensor on a 5 V reference has dead bands at both ends: below 4 % of the reference counts as low or open, 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms (about 3 s), engine not cranking, over 9 V, type A with the MIL after one trip. Saab names an open circuit or short to ground. With the clutch position unknown, cruise control, start-stop and starter release by the sensor are blocked.

causes.label: Signal wire open or shorted to ground
5 V reference of the sensor missing
Pedal sensor faulty internally
Connector corroded or pins loose

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control not working
Start-stop disabled, possibly no engine start

P0808.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0808.description: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0808 means the signal is too high. GM sets it above 96 % of the 5 V reference with the same 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms, type A with the MIL after one trip; Saab's 2012 9-3 above 4.8 V for longer than 0.6 s, with cruise control switched off. Typical causes are an open sensor ground or a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage.

causes.label: Sensor ground open
Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Pedal sensor faulty
Moisture or corrosion in the connector

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control not working
Start-stop disabled

P0809.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0809.description: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0809 is documented only for Ford's DPS6 (Fiesta from 2011, Focus from 2012): the motor that operates clutch A carries three Hall sensors, one per phase, and while the motor turns they must produce a fixed sequence; a wrong sequence sets the code. The clutch B counterpart is P087E. The module then loses confidence in the clutch position, so clutch A with the odd gears 1, 3 and 5 is restricted. GM and Saab do not use P0809; Ford publishes no thresholds.

causes.label: Clutch A actuator motor or its Hall sensors faulty
Loose contact at the actuator connector
Transmission module Hall evaluation faulty
Supply voltage dips

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Jerky or judder take-off
Limp mode, odd gears missing

P080A.title: Clutch Position Not Learned
P080A.description: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P080A means the learned clutch position is missing or implausible. On GM manual cars the factory learns the pedal position 'clutch fully pressed', and the engine module then tracks it as the clutch wears; a learned value outside 9.0–36.0 % of travel sets the code (250 ms, type A, one trip), a factory counter keeps the MIL off during assembly. Saab clears it by relearning with the scan tool. A relearn is needed after replacing the pedal sensor, master cylinder, clutch or engine module.

causes.label: Relearn not done after sensor, clutch or module replacement
Clutch badly worn or misadjusted
Pedal sensor misadjusted or wrongly fitted
Engine module reprogrammed or replaced

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Start-stop, cruise control or hill start assist disabled
Engine may start only with the pedal at the stop

P080B.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
P080B.description: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080B would be the range or performance fault of this circuit: electrically plausible, but outside the expected range for the command – for example a coil resistance outside its window, a partial short or contact resistance. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM's tables from 2006 to 2019 check the solenoid only electrically (P0803 open, P080C short to ground, P080D short to positive). CARB requires a functional check of outputs where feasible. The lockout may then work unreliably.

causes.label: Solenoid coil with shorted turns or resistance out of range
Retrofitted skip-shift eliminator with the wrong value
Corroded connector at the gearbox (contact resistance)
Control module or software

symptoms: Check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)
1-4 lockout works not at all or only sometimes
Otherwise no change in driving

P080C.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P080C.description: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080C means the control line is shorted to ground: with the driver off it should sit at battery voltage through the coil but reads low (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to ground). GM checks it from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips; the 2019 LT5 uses 20 of 25 samples and type A, one trip. In the 2015/16 tables P080C also covers an open circuit. A low-side short keeps the solenoid energized, so the lockout may stay active.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through to ground at gearbox or frame
Solenoid coil shorted to its housing
Connector corroded or water ingress
Older GM modules: circuit open or solenoid unplugged
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp
1-4 lockout permanently active or not working
1-4 lamp possibly unrelated to the lockout

P080D.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High
P080D.description: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080D means the control line is shorted to positive: with the low-side driver on, the line should be pulled to ground but reads high (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to the supply). The solenoid cannot be energized and the driver is protected or switched off. GM checks it only with the driver on, from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips in all tables from 2015 to 2019. Without power the solenoid does not lock, so 1 to 2 stays free.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage (damaged harness)
Solenoid coil with shorted turns (resistance near zero)
Substitute resistor ('eliminator') with too low a value
Engine module driver faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips
1-4 lockout not working
Otherwise no change in driving

P0810.title: Clutch Position Control Error
P0810.description: P0810 reports a control error of an electronically or hydraulically operated clutch: commanded and actual position differ too much or for too long. It is documented on Stellantis plug-in hybrids – Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH transmission – where it concerns the K0 disconnect clutch between engine and electric motor. According to the 2024 and 2025 bulletins the clutch adaptation ran at standstill or in electric mode, drive was lost until the next key cycle and the MIL came on; the cause was too tight setting parameters, fixed with new transmission software, partly together with P2885. On automated or dual-clutch gearboxes the same idea applies when the clutch actuator misses its target position.

causes.label: Control unit software with too tight parameters
Clutch actuator or hydraulics (pressure, valve) faulty
Clutch position sensor inaccurate
Wrong or aged fluid, worn clutch

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Transmission warning message
Loss of drive until the next key cycle

P0811.title: Excessive Clutch A Slippage
P0811.description: P0811 means clutch A slips too much while it should be closed – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 1 with the odd gears. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch; thresholds are not published. Audi's seven-speed S tronic DL382 (A4 to A7 and Q5, 2020–24) sets it intermittently together with P081E and input speed sensor codes, partly also clutch temperature too high; the cause was the transmission module calculating wrong slip, and the fix was a new module. Genuine slip from wear or overheating shows as flaring take-off and burnt fluid. The module limits torque, may lock out the affected half and go to limp mode.

causes.label: Transmission module calculating wrong slip (speed capture)
Clutch worn or overheated
Fluid burnt or wrong (wet clutch)
Clutch pressure or actuator too low
Input speed sensor faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning, limp mode
Engine flares, poor acceleration
Judder on take-off
Burning smell

P0812.title: Reverse Input Circuit
P0812.description: P0812 concerns the input 'reverse engaged' at the engine or transmission module – the reverse or back-up lamp switch on a manual gearbox, or the R contact of a selector. Modules check it for open or stuck states and against a second source such as a gear position sensor or the direction from speed sensors. A Honda patent describes this double detection: reverse counts only when switch and gear position sensor agree; if only one reports R, it is a fault and engine speed is limited. No manufacturer document with thresholds is available to us. Back-up lamps, reversing camera or parking aids may fail; on automated manual gearboxes reverse may be blocked. CARB lets such safety and comfort inputs run without the MIL.

causes.label: Reverse or back-up lamp switch faulty or misadjusted
Connector loose or wire broken (e.g. after clutch work)
Back-up lamp circuit fuse blown
Gear position sensor reporting the wrong position

symptoms: Back-up lamps never or always on
Reversing camera or parking aid does not switch on
Usually no check engine lamp

P0813.title: Reverse Output Circuit
P0813.description: P0813 concerns a signal 'reverse active' that a module puts out – usually the transmission module, on manual cars the engine or body module – for example to the back-up lamp relay, the reversing camera or the body module. Like other driver outputs it is checked by comparing commanded and actual state, which reveals an open circuit or a short. Saab's 2012 transmission module reports a short to positive on its park/neutral output in the same way. No manufacturer document with thresholds for the reverse output is available to us. Back-up lamps, camera or mirror tilt may stop working; driving itself is not affected, and CARB allows such outputs without the MIL.

causes.label: Wire from module to relay or body module open or shorted
Back-up lamp relay or connected load faulty
Connector corroded
Module output stage faulty

symptoms: Back-up lamps not working
Reversing camera or parking beeper does not activate
Stored code without driving effects

P0814.title: Transmission Range Display Circuit
P0814.description: P0814 concerns the drive or data circuit of the range display – the PRNDL or PRNDM display or lighting on the selector, sometimes in the instrument cluster. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: the electronic shift module stores P0814 with the MIL on, the selector lighting flickers or goes dark, and in a 2020 bulletin the lever could be moved out of park during cranking so that the engine stalled. The cause was software in the shift module, fixed by reflashing; a 2022 bulletin adds P081C. A wrong or missing range display matters for safety because the driver cannot reliably see P, R or N. No thresholds are published.

causes.label: Shift module software (Jeep Compass)
Connector or wire to the selector display or cluster
Display LED or selector module faulty
Range sensor or transmission module delivering an invalid range

symptoms: Range display on the selector flickers or stays dark
Check engine lamp (Jeep)
Lever can leave P during cranking, engine stalls (Jeep)

P0815.title: Upshift Switch Circuit
P0815.description: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0815 is the upshift switch. GM's 2019 and 2025 tables set it when 'tap up' stays on for more than 1 s in P or N, or permanently in a drive range; the 2018 hybrid table uses 2 s in P/N and 655 s in drive; type C without MIL. Ford's 6R80 and 6F35 SelectShift report a switch closed in P, R or N without MIL. On Saab's 9-4X with the 6T70 a Hall switch feeds a resistor network on one wire: a short to positive sets P0815 or P0816, a short to ground or an open sets P0826. Manual shifting is then disabled.

causes.label: Tap switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Signal wire shorted to positive
Selector assembly (Hall sensor, resistor network) faulty
Clockspring or steering wheel wiring (paddles)

symptoms: Manual up shifting not working
Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode
No check engine lamp

P0816.title: Downshift Switch Circuit
P0816.description: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0816 is the mirror of P0815 for the downshift switch. GM's 2025 table sets it when 'tap down' stays on for more than 1 s (100 ms raster, over 9 V), the 2018 hybrid table after 2 s in P/N or 655 s in drive, type C without MIL; Saab's 9-4X after 1 s in P/N or 10 minutes in a drive range; Ford's SelectShift when the switch is closed in P, R or N, without MIL. On selectors with a resistor network a short to positive in the downshift branch sets P0816. Manual shifting is disabled, automatic operation stays normal.

causes.label: Downshift switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Signal wire shorted to positive
Selector assembly faulty
Body or transmission module

symptoms: Manual down shifting not working
Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode
No check engine lamp

P0817.title: Starter Disable Circuit/Open
P0817.description: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P0817 is the general or open-circuit fault of this line. Saab sets it when the output reports 'start allowed' but the feedback shows 'off' for more than 100 ms, twice in a row, with 6–16 V and no limp mode; it rates the fault type D, without any lamp. The engine then cannot be started. Low and high are P081A and P081B; vehicles that send the start release over a bus often report similar faults as U codes or P0850.

causes.label: Starter disable wire to the body module open or shorted
Connector corroded or pins pushed back
Transmission module with built-in range switch faulty
Body module faulty

symptoms: Engine does not crank in P or N
Start possible in only one of the two ranges
No check engine lamp

P0818.title: Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit
P0818.description: P0818 concerns a switch input that reports whether the driveline is disconnected – on four-wheel-drive vehicles typically the neutral position of the transfer case or an axle disconnect, on hybrids a disconnect clutch between engine and transmission, as a Ford patent uses the term. It matters for OBD because in transfer case neutral the engine runs without load and wheel speed does not match the ratio, so misfire, ratio and vehicle speed monitors must know about it; CARB requires monitoring only then. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0818, and which of the two meanings applies cannot be proven. All-wheel drive or neutral may then be unavailable.

causes.label: Neutral or disconnect switch at the transfer case or axle faulty
Underbody wiring or connector corroded or damaged
Transfer case actuator does not reach its end position
Control module or software

symptoms: All-wheel drive or neutral cannot be selected
'Service 4WD' or similar warning
Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer)

P0819.title: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
P0819.description: P0819 is the plausibility check between the tap-up and tap-down switches and the range sensor: a shift request may only appear in the manual gate or in drive. If a tap switch reports in P, R or N, or taps arrive without the manual gate being detected, the correlation is broken. GM's 2019 tables and Ford's 2012 SelectShift run exactly this check but assign the fault to the switch concerned as P0815 or P0816; no manufacturer with its own P0819 is documented. Manual shifting would be disabled while automatic operation stays normal, without the MIL. Causes are a sticking tap switch, a misadjusted range sensor or selector cable, or the selector wiring.

causes.label: Tap switch sticking or faulty
Range sensor or selector sensor misadjusted or faulty
Selector cable misadjusted
Selector wiring or connectors

symptoms: Tap or manual mode not working
Range display partly wrong
No check engine lamp

P081A.title: Starter Disable Circuit Low
P081A.description: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081A means the start release line is too low – the output is shorted to ground or open. Saab's 2012 9-3 transmission module checks it in D, where the output must have a defined state, with 9–18 V, not in limp mode and continuously; no time threshold is published. Because the engine module then sees no 'P/N', the engine may not start.

causes.label: P/N line to the engine module shorted to ground
Line or connector open
Connector oxidized or pins pushed back
Transmission module output stage faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or only sometimes
Starter does not crank in P or N
No check engine lamp

P081B.title: Starter Disable Circuit High
P081B.description: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081B means the start release line stays at positive, so the 'P/N' level is present in a drive range. Saab's 2012 9-3 checks it only outside P and N, with 9–18 V and not in limp mode. A short to positive could in principle allow a start in gear; the diagnosis catches it, and Saab names as the effect that the engine may not start because the release is refused.

causes.label: P/N line shorted to positive (chafed against a supply wire)
Moisture or corrosion in the connector
Transmission module output stage faulty

symptoms: Engine does not start or starts unreliably
Start release in the wrong range possible (safety risk)
No check engine lamp

P081C.title: Park Input Circuit
P081C.description: P081C concerns the input 'park position' – the P contact of the selector or shift module, or the park pawl feedback – which controls switching off the ignition, key release, starter release and the 'not in park' warning. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: a 2022 bulletin lists P081C with the MIL on, with 'Vehicle not in Park' shown although P is engaged; the car cannot be switched off, modules stay awake and the battery drains. The cause was shift module software, fixed by reflashing. The check is a circuit or plausibility test of the P signal against the range sensor; no thresholds are published.

causes.label: Shift module software (Jeep Compass)
P contact or selector switch faulty or misadjusted
Selector cable misadjusted
Wire or connector

symptoms: 'Not in park' message although P is engaged
Ignition cannot be switched off, battery drains
Check engine lamp (Jeep)

P081D.title: Neutral Input Circuit
P081D.description: P081D concerns the input 'neutral' – the N contact of the selector or range switch, on manual cars a neutral switch or sensor for start-stop. Neutral serves for starter release, idle control without load, start-stop release and enabling other diagnostics. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the range sensor or speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P081D; its sister P081C is documented on the Jeep Compass, and Saab's range switch shows that P and N are the two start positions. The engine may then not start in N, start-stop is disabled and idle diagnostics may be suspended.

causes.label: Neutral contact, range switch or neutral sensor faulty or misadjusted
Selector or shift cable misadjusted
Wire or connector
Control module or software

symptoms: Engine does not start in N (only in P)
Start-stop not working
Range display does not show N

P081E.title: Excessive Clutch B Slippage
P081E.description: P081E is the counterpart to P0811 for clutch B – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 2 with the even gears and reverse, which Audi calls 'clutch 2'. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch and flags slip above its limit. Audi's DL382 S tronic (2020–24) sets it intermittently with P0811 and input speed codes; the bulletins report a transmission malfunction and 'reverse gear unavailable', and the fix was a new transmission module with improved parts from late 2023. A failed clutch 2 typically means no reverse and no even gears.

causes.label: Transmission module speed capture faulty
Clutch 2 worn or overheated
Fluid or pressure

P0830.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit
P0830.description: Clutch pedal switches A and B are digital inputs of manual gearboxes: they release the starter only with the pedal pressed, switch off cruise control and tell start-stop whether the clutch is open. P0836.description: The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs. Older cars used a wire with a voltage or duty-cycle signal, hence the low and high variants; today it is a CAN message, where pure loss of communication sets U0121 or U0415 instead. California's OBD rule counts traction control as a safety-only system that may be exempted, so these codes normally carry no MIL. P0858 means a wired signal stays below its lower limit: short to ground, an open line without pull-up, or a sending module without power. No maker documents the code; the request is discarded and traction control switched off.

symptoms: Traction or stability control lamp on, system switched off
No torque reduction when wheels spin

P085A.title: Gear Shift Control Module B Communication Circuit
P085A.description: Gear shift control modules A and B are selector modules of shift-by-wire systems, such as Audi's selector lever J587 or Stellantis' rotary shift module. Modules on CAN report lost communication as U0103 or invalid data as U0404 instead; GM uses its own codes. P085A is the general fault of the link to module B: no or no valid frames. P0863.title: TCM Communication Circuit
P0863.description: The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL. On CAN cars, loss of the gearbox module sets U0101 or U0402 instead. P0863 is the general fault of this link without telling range, low or high apart. No maker documents it on its own. Without the link the engine module receives no gearbox status, and a MIL request from the gearbox gets lost.

Gearbox module faulty
Input of the engine module faulty

symptoms: Check engine lamp on
Gearbox warning or limp mode possible

P0867.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure
P0867.description: P0867 to P0869 cover the system or line pressure of the gearbox as a whole: a pressure sensor measures it and the control module compares it with the pressure it commands. Faults of the sensor circuit itself have their own codes (Chrysler 68RFE P0932 ff), the single switches A to H have theirs (P0840 ff). Thresholds are not published; the codes are documented in bulletins for the Ram 68RFE and for the Tremec dual clutch of Corvette C8 and Maserati MC20. P0867 is the general pressure fault. GM's Corvette bulletin reads it as 'no system pressure': the pump delivers nothing or the fluid is almost gone, so valve cleaning is pointless and the gearbox needs a mechanical check. The car may lose drive completely.

Fluid pump or its drive faulty
Pressure regulator or relief valve sticking
System pressure sensor faulty

symptoms: Transmission warning lamp or MIL on
Weak or no drive
Limp mode, car may be stranded

P086A.title: Neutral Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P086A.description: Neutral position sensor A is a position sensor, usually a three-wire Hall sensor, on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox. Audi uses it as sender G701 on Q3 and A3, GM on the 2019 Corvette ZR1 with its 7-speed manual, where these codes suspend the gear ratio checks. P086A is the circuit fault: the signal is missing, typically an open supply or signal wire. Audi's bulletin for the sister codes P086D/P086E found the supply wires to G701 too short and lengthened them. Start-stop stays off.

Corroded connector low on the gearbox

symptoms: Start-stop not working

P0870.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit
P0870.description: Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. They are more widespread than A and B: GM's 6L80/6L90 and 6T40/6T70 six-speeds put switch C on the 2-6 brake and D on the 1-2-3-4 clutch, Allison uses them for its third shift valve and its reverse switch, Ram's RFE gearboxes for the clutch pressure switches in the solenoid block. P087A.title: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit
P087A.description: Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). P0880.title: TCM Power Input Signal
P0880.description: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Weak battery, charging fault, poor ground
Gearbox module faulty

symptoms: MIL on
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Harsh engagement into D or R

P0881.title: TCM Power Input Signal Range/Performance
P0881.description: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. P0882.title: TCM Power Input Signal Low
P0882.description: The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. P0883.title: TCM Power Input Signal High

P0885.description: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. A dead relay leaves all solenoids without power, so the gearbox drops into its hydraulic emergency gear. P0885 means the coil circuit is open; the module checks its relay driver output at key-on. Wire between relay and module open, connector or fuse box contact
Fuse of the relay coil blown
Module software (FCA 948TE reflash)

symptoms: MIL on
Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting
Harsh engagement into D or R

P0886.title: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P0886.description: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P088A.title: Transmission Fluid Filter Deteriorated
P088A.description: Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. Its filter life monitor judges the pressure drop across the filter circuit; in Allison's patent a differential pressure valve operates a switch with temperature-dependent time limits. P088A, called 'filter maintenance alert' by Allison, is the early warning: the wrench symbol flashes. A faulty main valve body in some 3000/4000 units triggered it early (field action 2019FA07). Heavy contamination from clutch wear

Faulty main valve body (Allison serial range)

P088B.title: Transmission Fluid Filter Very Deteriorated

Faulty main valve body (Allison)

P088C.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit Low
P088C.description: The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code. GM rates it type C without MIL; from 2019 a service message appears. P0801 is the open circuit. Water or corrosion in the gearbox connector
Engine module driver faulty

Service message (GM from 2019), no MIL

P0891.title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
P0891.description: Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. P0892.title: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Intermittent

P0893.title: Multiple Gears Engaged
P0893.description: P0893 means more shift elements are applied than the commanded gear allows, so the gearbox binds up. P0894.title: Transmission Component Slipping
P0894.description: P0894 reports slip of a gearbox component, found by comparing speeds. P0895.title: Shift Time Too Short
P0895.description: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. No maker could be found using these generic codes; Saab's 1994 900 automatic monitored the same with its own code P1832, a window of 0.3 to 1.3 s and a limp program. P0895 means the shift completes faster than the window: clutch pressure too high or applied too early, giving a harsh shift.

Valve body: sticking spool, faulty damper or accumulator
Wrong fluid or level

Transmission warning lamp
Limp mode possible

P0896.title: Shift Time Too Long
P0896.description: Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. P0897.title: Transmission Fluid Deteriorated

Correct calculation assumes approved fluid (TES 295/668).

causes.label: Fluid change interval exceeded
Fluid changed without resetting the oil life monitor
Heavy duty (heat, stop-and-go, retarder) shortens calculated life
Prognostics disabled afterwards (Allison special case)

symptoms: CHECK TRANS lamp on
TRANS SERVICE or wrench indicator after each start beforehand
Driving usually normal

P0898.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Low
P0898.description: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866. P0898 means the request wire stays at ground: a short to ground or, with active-high logic, a gearbox module without power. The engine module can then not tell a real request from a wiring fault. No maker documents the code; Subaru's P0865 is the closest documented equivalent.

causes.label: MIL request wire shorted to ground
Engine or gearbox module connector corroded
Gearbox module output faulty

symptoms: MIL on
Gearbox faults may not be indicated correctly

P0899.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit High
P0899.description: The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866. P0899 means the request wire stays high: an open line held up by the engine module's pull-up, a short to voltage or, with active-low logic, a gearbox module without power. No maker documents the code; Subaru's equivalent is P0866, set after more than 3 s high with MIL after two trips.

causes.label: Wire open (pull-up in the engine module)
Short to voltage
Gearbox module without power or ground
Gearbox module faulty

symptoms: MIL on
Gearbox faults may not be reported
Limp mode as well if the gearbox module has no power

P089A.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089A.description: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089A, the general circuit fault of X sensor 2, is used by no maker found; GM reports circuit faults through duty-cycle low or high and frequency errors under P089B.

causes.label: Wire or connector at the selector module open
Sensor 2 in the selector faulty
Spilled liquid in the centre console

symptoms: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Range selection delayed or limited
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089B.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P089B.description: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. GM sets P089B when X sensor 2 reports a lever travel outside the gate (tolerance 5.5 % of duty cycle), its frequency is faulty, or it differs from sensor 1 by more than 12 %; 3 of 4 samples every 25 ms. Type B, MIL after two trips.

causes.label: Sensor 2 in the selector assembly faulty or drifting
Selector mechanism worn or bent
Loose contact or interference on the PWM line
Liquid in the console

symptoms: MIL after two trips
Range selection delayed or limited
Only P available if both sensors fail

P089C.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P089C.description: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. GM sets P089C when the duty cycle of X sensor 2 falls below 17 % (2019) or 5 % (XT4 and 2025): signal wire to ground, sensor without output or missing supply. Type B, MIL after two trips; sensor 1 carries on.

causes.label: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor 2 faulty
Supply of the selector sensor open
Connector corrosion from spilled drinks

symptoms: MIL after two trips
Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089D.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit High
P089D.description: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. GM sets P089D when the duty cycle of X sensor 2 rises above 88 % (2019) or 95 % (XT4 and 2025): open signal wire with pull-up, short to voltage or a sensor stuck high. Type B, MIL after two trips.

causes.label: Signal wire open (pull-up) or shorted to voltage
Sensor 2 faulty
Sensor ground open

symptoms: MIL after two trips
Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P089E.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P089E.description: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089E, for jumping or briefly dropping X sensor 2 signals, is used by no maker found; GM catches signal disturbances through the frequency error under P089B. The counterpart for sensor 1, P0823, is unused as well.

causes.label: Loose contact at the selector connector
Sensor 2 with internal dropouts
Wire chafed in the console

symptoms: Selector warning at times
Range selection hesitates sporadically

P089F.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit
P089F.description: Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089F, the general circuit fault of Y sensor 2, is used by no maker found; GM reports that sensor under P08A0 to P08A2. In GM's patent a sensor counts as invalid as a whole once its X or Y value fails.

causes.label: Wire or connector at the selector module open
Sensor 2 faulty
Corrosion from liquid in the console

symptoms: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster
Range selection delayed or limited
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P08A0.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance
P08A0.description: Sensor 2 is the redundant second Hall sensor that reports the Y-axis travel of an electronic selector lever as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses it in its electronic range selection (ECM and ICCM tables 2019–2025, Cadillac XT4 among them). P08A0 is set when sensor 2 reports a lever path outside the shifter gate (tolerance 5.5 %, ICCM 6–11 % of duty cycle), its frequency check fails, or it disagrees with Y sensor 1 by more than 12 %. Debounce is 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms (2025: 10 of 12). Type B, MIL after two trips. Low/High of the same sensor are P08A1/P08A2. GM's patent lets the other sensor carry on; only when both are invalid may the module ask for park.

causes.label: Sensor 2 in the selector assembly drifting or faulty
Selector mechanism worn, bent or binding, lever leaves its nominal path
Loose contact or interference on the PWM signal line
Spilled liquid in the centre console

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Shift lever message or occasional unaccepted range selection
Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over

P08A1.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Low
P08A1.description: The selector lever's Y-axis sensor 2 is one of two redundant Hall sensors that send the lever travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM documents P08A1 for its electronic range selection: the code sets when the measured duty cycle of Y sensor 2 drops below 17 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or below 5 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025), checked 3 of 4 samples at 25 ms or 10 of 12 in later years. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a dead sensor output. Type B, MIL after two trips. Unlike P08A0 this is a pure signal limit, not a plausibility check; high is P08A2. Sensor 1 keeps the selector working.

causes.label: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Sensor supply open or connector backed out
Sensor 2 in the selector assembly without output
Connector corrosion from liquid in the console

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Shifter warning message in the cluster
Normally no change in driving, sensor 1 takes over

P08A2.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit High
P08A2.description: Y sensor 2 is the backup Hall sensor of an electronic selector lever and reports the lever's Y-axis travel as a PWM duty cycle. GM uses P08A2 in its electronic range selection and sets it when the duty cycle of Y sensor 2 rises above 88 % (2019 ECM and ICCM tables) or above 95 % (Cadillac XT4 2019, ECM tables 2023–2025); 3 failures in 4 samples at 25 ms, in later calibrations 10 of 12. A signal line shorted to voltage, an open ground or an internal sensor fault are the usual reasons. Type B, MIL after two trips. Range/performance and low are P08A0 and P08A1; sensor 1 of the same axis reports via P082D to P082F. With one sensor still valid, the lever stays usable.

causes.label: Sensor 2 signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Sensor ground open or high resistance
Internal fault of sensor 2 in the selector assembly

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives
Shifter warning message in the cluster
Range selection normally still works via sensor 1

P08A3.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 2 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08A3.description: This code covers short dropouts or jumps in the signal of the second, redundant Y-axis sensor of an electronic selector lever. No manufacturer documents P08A3 publicly. GM, the only proven user of this sensor family, uses only range/performance, low and high (P08A0 to P08A2) in all OBD tables from 2016 to 2025 and catches an unsteady PWM signal through the frequency check inside P08A0. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires input components to be monitored for circuit faults and plausibility. GM's patent on two redundant lever sensors explains why a second sensor exists: if one becomes invalid, the other keeps range selection alive. Expect loose contacts in the console harness; the MIL status depends on the maker.

causes.label: Loose or fretting contact at the selector connector
Harness chafed by console or lever movement
Sensor 2 with intermittent internal fault

symptoms: Stored fault that comes and goes, often without driver complaint
Occasional shifter warning message
Possibly check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A4.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A4.description: An electronic selector lever with redundant sensing measures the X axis with two sensors. P08A4 means the two X readings no longer agree although each may be within its own limits. No manufacturer documents P08A4 publicly. GM, which runs dual PWM lever sensors, folds this comparison into the range/performance codes: P089B sets when X sensor 2 differs from sensor 1 by more than 12 % duty cycle. GM patents describe the principle: each sensor is checked against the gate and against its partner, and on disagreement the module trusts the more robust signal or commands neutral or park. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) demands such plausibility monitoring. Y-axis counterpart is P08A5, the whole system P08A6.

causes.label: One of the two X sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path

symptoms: Shifter warning message
Range selection refused or vehicle held in neutral or park
Check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A5.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P08A5.description: P08A5 is the Y-axis twin of P08A4: the two redundant sensors that measure the selector lever's Y travel disagree beyond a calibrated limit. No manufacturer documents P08A5 publicly. In GM's electronic range selection the same check exists but is reported as range/performance: P08A0 sets when Y sensor 2 and Y sensor 1 differ by more than 12 % duty cycle, Type B. GM's patents show why redundancy matters: a disagreeing pair is resolved by trusting the more fault-tolerant signal, and if that is not possible the module selects neutral or park. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires such rationality checks for inputs. For the driver this means a refused or held range; repairs usually replace the selector assembly.

causes.label: One of the two Y sensors drifting
Magnet carrier or lever mechanism shifted or worn
Contact resistance on one sensor's signal path

symptoms: Shifter warning message
Range selection refused or vehicle held in neutral or park
Check engine light, depending on the manufacturer

P08A6.title: Gear Lever Position Sensor System - Multiple Sensor Correlation
P08A6.description: Here the module compares the combined gear lever position information with other evidence and finds no consistent picture. Two makers document it. FCA/Stellantis sets P08A6 in the PCM of 6-speed manual Jeeps such as the Wrangler JL as the all-gear-sensor check: the sensed gear is compared with a learned top-gear engine-to-road-speed ratio, so larger tyres trigger it until that ratio is relearned in sixth at 40–80 mph; a 4Low issue and software updates are also known, with MIL. Maserati's electronic shift module stores P08A6-64 for signal plausibility, leaving no gear selectable. Unlike P08A4/P08A5 it concerns the whole sensor system, not one sensor pair.

causes.label: Tyre size changed without relearning the top-gear ratio (FCA manual)
Control module software needing an update
Modified transfer case gearing, fault only in 4Low
Internal fault or connector problem of the electronic shift module

symptoms: Check engine light
Start-stop and gear indicator disabled, clutch overheat or service transmission message
On shift-by-wire, no gear can be selected

P08A7.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit/Open
P08A7.description: Sensor A is the analog or PWM sensor that reports how far the clutch pedal of a manual car is pressed; the engine controller needs it for start-stop, cruise control, gear detection and starter release. P08A7 is the general circuit or open-wire fault of that sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: GM folds an open circuit into its low-signal code P08A9, and Ford lists only P08A9/P08AA for sensor A. Saab's 2012 9-3 used the older P0806 as a comparable circuit fault (Check Engine, cruise control off). Range/performance, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes P08A8–P08AB. Expect a warning lamp and disabled start-stop or cruise control until the wiring or sensor is repaired.

causes.label: Loose connector or broken wire at the pedal sensor (pedal box wiring flexes with every clutch stroke)
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor A
Missing 5 V reference or sensor ground
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Start-stop and cruise control unavailable
Engine may not crank if the starter release relies on the sensor

P08A8.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P08A8.description: P08A8 flags a clutch pedal sensor whose signal is electrically valid but contradicts how the car is actually driving. GM uses it on manual cars since model year 2018 (before: P0806), e.g. the LV7 1.4 L engine and the 2019 Corvette ZR1 (LT5): when engine speed to output shaft speed shows that a gear is engaged and transmitting torque, but the pedal reads as pressed, the filtered position error must stay below 4 %. Enabled above 4.3 mph (LT5: 5.6 mph), not in 4WD low, torque above a table, no circuit, crank or speed sensor faults; Type A, MIL after one trip. Circuit faults are P08A9/P08AA. Typical result: start-stop and cruise control off, and the engine computer may misjudge clutch state.

causes.label: Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket, so its reading no longer matches pedal travel
Worn or drifting sensor track giving an offset signal
Driver resting a foot on the clutch pedal, or a floor mat holding it down
Corroded connector adding resistance to signal or ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Start-stop and cruise control switched off
Rev-matching or hill-start functions may be disabled

P08A9.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P08A9.description: The sensor is designed with dead bands at both ends, so a signal near 0 V can only come from a fault. GM sets P08A9 when the signal stays below 4 % of the 5 V reference (low voltage or open circuit) for 400 of 500 samples taken every 12.5 ms, with the engine not cranking and system voltage above 9 V (10 V in some 2018 tables); Type A, MIL after one trip. GM used P0807 for this before 2018 and lists P08A9 for the LV7, the 2019 Corvette ZR1 and its 2018 OBDG04 engines. Ford's 2020–23 gasoline summary uses P08A9 for cars with dual PWM pedal sensors or a single analog sensor plus switches, detected in under a second. The high-side counterpart is P08AA; sensor B low is P08B6.

causes.label: Signal wire chafed through and shorted to ground in the pedal area
Open signal wire or missing 5 V reference (connector off, broken wire)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Shared 5 V reference pulled down by another sensor on the same circuit

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Start-stop and cruise control unavailable
Engine may refuse to crank on vehicles that release the starter via the sensor

P08AA.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P08AA.description: P08AA is the mirror image of P08A9: the pedal sensor signal climbs into the upper dead band that a healthy sensor never reaches. GM's threshold is above 96 % of the 5 V reference for 400 of 500 samples at 12.5 ms, engine not cranking, system voltage above 9 V; Type A, MIL after one trip. It replaced GM's pre-2018 P0808 and appears in the LV7, 2019 Corvette ZR1 and 2018 OBDG04 tables. Ford's 2020–23 gasoline summary lists P08AA for both its dual PWM and single analog clutch pedal sensor layouts, flagged in under a second. A lost sensor ground or a signal shorted to the reference are the usual triggers. Sensor B high is P08B7; the driver mostly loses start-stop and cruise control.

causes.label: Open sensor ground wire or corroded ground pin
Signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage
Failed clutch pedal position sensor A
Faulty sensor input in the engine control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on after one trip
Start-stop and cruise control disabled
Clutch status shown incorrectly in scan tool data

P08AB.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08AB.description: P08AB is meant for a clutch pedal sensor A signal that jumps, drops out briefly or changes faster than a foot could move the pedal, without staying out of range long enough for the low or high codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's published tables for the same sensor use only P08A8, P08A9, P08AA and P08AC, and its low/high checks need 400 of 500 bad samples, so short dropouts would go unnoticed there; Ford names only low, high and A/B correlation. CARB requires such inputs to be checked for circuit faults and plausibility. In practice the cause is usually a loose connector or a wire that breaks inside its insulation as the pedal moves. Start-stop and cruise control may cut out intermittently.

causes.label: Loose or worn terminals in the pedal sensor connector
Wire breaking inside its insulation where the harness flexes with the pedal
Worn sensor track causing signal dropouts at certain pedal positions
Moisture or corrosion in the footwell connector

symptoms: Start-stop or cruise control cutting out intermittently
Warning lamp that comes and goes
Erratic clutch pedal value in scan tool data while the pedal is held still

P08AC.title: Clutch Pedal Position Not Learned
P08AC.description: The engine controller has to know at which pedal position the clutch is fully released or disengaged. GM teaches the fully applied position at the factory and then adapts it over time to clutch wear. P08AC is set when this learned value falls outside a window (LV7 1.4 L: 7–33 %, 2019 Corvette ZR1: 9–36 % of travel) or when the manufacturer's enable counter shows the learn was never completed; 250 ms loop, Type A, MIL after one trip. Before 2018 GM used P080A. After replacing the sensor, pedal parts, clutch or ECM, a relearn with a scan tool is needed; FCA, for example, issued a Renegade bulletin calling for a clutch pedal sensor learn. Circuit faults (P08A9/P08AA) must be cleared first.

causes.label: Relearn not performed after replacing the sensor, clutch parts or engine control module
Learned position drifted out of the allowed window (worn clutch, wrong pedal stop, air in hydraulics)
Learn procedure aborted, for example by low battery voltage
Faulty or misaligned clutch pedal sensor preventing a valid learn

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Start-stop, cruise control or automatic parking brake release not working as expected

P08AD.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P08AD.description: A neutral position sensor tells the engine module whether a manual gearbox is in neutral, which start-stop, remote start and rev matching rely on. Sensor B is a second sensor or channel next to sensor A (P086A ff). P08AD flags an open or otherwise faulty sensor B circuit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi (sender G701) and GM (Corvette LT5) are only known to use the A codes. A GM patent shows why a B channel exists: two Hall sensors on the shift shaft give a PWM signal, and in neutral both must read the same. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring of such inputs. Expected effect: start-stop stays off; MIL status depends on the maker.

causes.label: Wire to the sensor broken or stretched by shift shaft movement
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded
Sensor B open internally

symptoms: Start-stop no longer switches the engine off
Start system warning in the cluster
Driving normally unaffected

P08AE.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08AE.description: Sensor B is the second neutral sensor or channel on the shift shaft of a manual gearbox, complementing sensor A (P086A ff). P08AE means its signal is electrically present but implausible: it stays outside the expected window, does not change when gears are engaged, or reports neutral while the gear ratio says otherwise. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Audi's G701 and GM's LT5 Corvette are only known to use the A codes. Per a GM patent the neutral sensor is a Hall sensor pair with a PWM output that changes with every gear, so such a plausibility check is possible. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires rationality monitoring of inputs. Start-stop is usually disabled; repair often means adjusting or replacing the sensor.

causes.label: Sensor B or its magnet misaligned after gearbox work
Sensor B drifting or faulty
Worn shift shaft or detent giving an unclear neutral position

symptoms: Start-stop unavailable
Start system or gear indicator message in the cluster
No noticeable change while driving

P08AF.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08AF.description: The signal of neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel of a manual gearbox, has fallen below its lower electrical limit. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a missing sensor supply or a sensor without output. No manufacturer documents P08AF publicly; the A-sensor codes are documented by Audi (sender G701, three-wire Hall sensor) and by GM on the LT5 Corvette. A GM patent describes the sensor as two Hall elements on the shift shaft feeding a PWM signal to the engine module. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires low/high circuit monitoring of such inputs. High is P08B0, the A-sensor equivalent P086C. Start-stop is usually blocked; the MIL status is left to the manufacturer.

causes.label: Signal wire chafed and shorted to ground
Sensor supply open
Sensor B without output
Water or corrosion in the connector at the gearbox

symptoms: Start-stop no longer works
Start system warning in the cluster
Fault stored without driving complaint

P08B0.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B0.description: P08B0 reports that the signal of neutral position sensor B on a manual gearbox is above its upper electrical limit. With a three-wire Hall sensor this usually points to an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage. No manufacturer documents P08B0 publicly. For the A sensor Audi does: the 2019–20 Q3 and 2022–23 A3 store P086D/P086E because the wires to sender G701 were too short and were pulled apart by shifting, fixed by lengthening them 20 mm; the same harness logic applies to a B sensor. A GM patent explains the dual-Hall neutral sensor with PWM output. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring. Low is P08AF; start-stop is typically off.

causes.label: Signal or ground wire pulled apart, harness too short
Signal wire shorted to voltage
Sensor B open internally

symptoms: Start-stop does not switch the engine off
Start system warning in the cluster
Fault may come and go with gear changes

P08B1.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B1.description: Neutral position sensor B, the second neutral sensor or channel on a manual gearbox's shift shaft, delivers a signal that drops out or jumps for short moments. No manufacturer documents P08B1 publicly. The closest documented case is on the A sensor: Audi's bulletin for the 2019–20 Q3 and 2022–23 A3 traces P086D/P086E to wires to sender G701 that were too short, so every gear change strained them; lengthening by 20 mm cures it. A Dura patent notes that a neutral signal must persist for a minimum time before start-stop may stop the engine, so a flickering sensor blocks the function. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires circuit monitoring. Steady faults appear as P08AD, P08AF or P08B0.

causes.label: Wire strained or partly broken by gearbox movement
Loose or fretting connector contact
Sensor B with intermittent internal fault

symptoms: Start-stop works only now and then
Occasional start system message
Fault returns after clearing without visible cause

P08B2.title: Neutral Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P08B2.description: On a manual gearbox with two neutral sensors or two channels, the engine module compares A and B. P08B2 means they disagree: one reports neutral, the other a gear, or their values differ beyond a calibrated limit, while each may look fine electrically. No manufacturer documents P08B2 publicly. A GM patent describes exactly this layout: two Hall sensors with their own magnets on the shift shaft, whose PWM outputs must be identical in neutral as an integrity check. Audi's G701 and GM's LT5 Corvette use only the A codes. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) requires rationality monitoring of inputs. Because neutral cannot be confirmed, start-stop and remote start stay off; usual fix is aligning or replacing the sensor.

causes.label: One of the two neutral sensors drifting or faulty
Magnet on the shift shaft shifted or sensor misaligned after repair
Neutral position not relearned after component replacement

symptoms: Start-stop unavailable
Start system warning in the cluster
Gear indicator may be blank or wrong

P08B3.title: Neutral Position Sensor B Not Learned
P08B3.description: Analog neutral sensors report a position value, and the control module must learn which value means neutral to cover part and fitting tolerances. P08B3 says no valid learned value exists for sensor B, typically after replacing the sensor, gearbox or module, after a software update, or after an aborted learn. No manufacturer documents P08B3 publicly; the A counterpart P086F is used by GM on the LT5 Corvette. A Schaeffler patent describes the learn: the driver engages neutral and the gears, and a run is rejected if the reading wanders too much in its roughly one-second window. FCA notes a neutral sensor learn procedure after service that restores cruise control. CARB 1968.2 (e)(15) applies. Fix is usually a relearn by scan tool.

causes.label: Learn procedure not done after sensor, gearbox or module replacement
Learn run aborted, lever unsteady or linkage misadjusted
Learned values erased by software update or module reset
Sensor mounted outside the learnable range or faulty

symptoms: Start-stop unavailable
Cruise control may be inoperative
Appears right after a repair or software update

P08B4.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit/Open
P08B4.description: Some manual cars read the clutch pedal with two independent sensors so a single failure can be detected; Ford's 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary describes such a dual PWM layout. Sensor B is the second channel. P08B4 is the general circuit or open-wire fault of that second sensor. No manufacturer documents this code publicly: Ford uses only P08B6/P08B7 for sensor B plus P08B9 for the A/B comparison, and GM's tables cover sensor A alone. The code therefore rests on CARB's requirement to monitor such inputs for circuit faults. Sensor A's counterpart is P08A7. As long as sensor A is healthy the controller can usually still judge the pedal, but start-stop is often locked out until the fault is fixed.

causes.label: Loose connector or broken wire on the sensor B channel
Internal fault in clutch pedal position sensor B (often a shared housing with sensor A)
Missing supply or ground for sensor B
Faulty sensor B input in the engine control module

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Correlation code P08B9 may be stored as well

P08B5.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P08B5.description: P08B5 covers a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal lies within its electrical limits but is implausible on its own, for example stuck at one value while the pedal moves or not matching the driving state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's dual PWM pedal sensor layout files any disagreement between the two channels under P08B9 rather than a B-only plausibility code, and GM applies the comparable in-gear plausibility check only to sensor A (P08A8: error above 4 % while a gear is engaged). CARB requires plausibility monitoring for inputs used by other diagnostics. If a manufacturer uses it, expect start-stop to be disabled; the clutch itself keeps working because it is hydraulically operated.

causes.label: Sensor B drifting or worn so its value no longer follows pedal travel
Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket
Corrosion adding resistance in the sensor B circuit

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Start-stop or cruise control unavailable

P08B6.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P08B6.description: P08B6 means the signal of the second clutch pedal sensor has dropped below its valid range. Ford lists it in the 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary under dual PWM clutch sensors, together with P08A9/P08AA for sensor A, P08B7 for sensor B high and P08B9 for the A/B comparison; monitoring runs continuously and needs less than one second to flag a fault. Ford does not mark the code as non-MIL, unlike its clutch switch codes. For a PWM sensor, low usually means the output is stuck at ground (no pulses or 0 % duty cycle), caused by a short to ground, a lost supply or a dead sensor. GM's published tables have no sensor B. The driver mainly notices a warning lamp and missing start-stop.

causes.label: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Lost supply voltage to sensor B (open wire, connector off)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
P08B9 correlation code may set alongside

P08B7.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P08B7.description: P08B7 is set when the second clutch pedal sensor reports a value above its valid range. Ford uses it on vehicles with two PWM clutch pedal sensors, as listed in its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary next to P08B6 (sensor B low), P08A9/P08AA (sensor A) and P08B9 (A/B correlation); the check is continuous and decides within one second. The clutch switch codes on the same page are marked non-MIL, the sensor codes are not. With a PWM output, high typically means the line is held at its pull-up level (100 % duty cycle), which points to an open signal or ground wire or a short to voltage. GM's published tables cover sensor A only. Effect for the driver: warning lamp, start-stop locked out.

causes.label: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B, leaving the input at its pull-up level
Sensor B signal shorted to a voltage source
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Sensor B reading pinned at maximum in scan tool data

P08B8.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P08B8.description: P08B8 is intended for a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal drops out briefly or jumps without staying out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford, the only maker found to publish sensor B codes, lists just low (P08B6), high (P08B7) and the A/B comparison (P08B9) for its dual PWM pedal sensors, so short glitches there would most likely surface as a correlation fault; GM covers sensor A only. CARB requires circuit and plausibility monitoring of such inputs. Likely culprits are worn connector terminals or a wire fatiguing where the harness moves with the pedal. Sensor A's counterpart is P08AB. Drivers may see start-stop drop out now and then.

causes.label: Loose or worn terminals in the sensor B connector
Wire fatiguing where the harness flexes with pedal movement
Sensor B producing glitches internally

symptoms: Start-stop dropping out intermittently
Warning lamp that comes and goes

P08B9.title: Clutch Pedal Position Sensor A/B Correlation
P08B9.description: P08B9 is stored when two independent measurements of the clutch pedal disagree. Ford uses it in two ways per its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary: with dual PWM sensors it compares sensor A with sensor B and decides within a second; with a single analog sensor plus two clutch switches it covers an in-range rationality fault or any switch-related mismatch, the switch part being judged over about 40 clutch cycles at different speeds. FCA patented a similar cross-check of the pedal sensor against the clutch interlock switch, which disables electronic stop-start on a mismatch and cannot always tell which part failed. Circuit faults of each sensor have their own codes (P08A9/P08AA, P08B6/P08B7).

causes.label: One of the two sensors drifting or worn so the channels no longer agree
Sticking or misadjusted clutch switch on systems with one sensor plus switches
Corroded connector or wiring adding resistance to one channel
Sensor assembly or pedal stop misaligned after repairs

symptoms: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Cruise control unavailable

P08BA.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L
P08BA.description: Base code for the twelfth pressure control solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve carries the letter L is up to the manufacturer. Toyota is the one documented user: bulletin T-SB-0094-24 for the 2024 Tacoma and Tacoma Hybrid lists it as P08BA71, actuator stuck, next to the stuck faults of solenoids A, C, D, G and H and a torque converter clutch stuck off. Because Toyota reports the fault type through the suffix, the stuck valve sits under this base code rather than under P08BB/P08BC. The MIL comes on. For trucks built before the production change Toyota's fix is a new transmission with torque converter, on the hybrid also the hybrid module. GM's Corvette dual clutch tables contain no L code.

causes.label: Solenoid or its control valve sticking inside the valve body
Internal transmission fault from production, debris spreading through the hydraulics
Contaminated or wrong transmission fluid
Connector or harness fault at the solenoid

symptoms: Check engine light on
Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Transmission may hold a substitute gear

P08BB.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Performance/Stuck Off
P08BB.description: Set when pressure control solenoid L is commanded but the pressure or shift element it serves does not respond, i.e. the valve acts as if it were stuck in its off state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Toyota, the only known user of letter L, reports a stuck valve as P08BA with suffix 71 instead. The closest documented analogue is GM's P08C4 for solenoid M on the Corvette dual clutch, where an intrusive routine moves the shift rods slightly and flags the valve when the expected rod travel stays below 100 µm. CARB requires such functional checks for transmission solenoids. P08BC is the opposite fault, P08BF to P08C2 cover the circuit. The driver notices missing or harsh shifts.

causes.label: Valve spool held closed by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Leaking seal or circuit downstream of the valve

symptoms: Check engine light on
Missing, slipping or delayed shifts
Possible substitute gear operation

P08BC.title: Pressure Control Solenoid L Stuck On
P08BC.description: Set when pressure control solenoid L keeps applying pressure although the control module has commanded it off, so the element it feeds stays loaded. No manufacturer publishes this code. Toyota, the only documented user of letter L, files a stuck valve under P08BA71 instead.
